rationale:
Evidence. Iteration 5 (base_speed 1.1, kd 0.5, kp 3.0, sensors at y=0.065 spanning x=±0.042, mass 0.5) is the best design so far at 711. Its oval finished 20/20 and its s-bend finished 18/20. Its slalom never finished: 0/20, progress 0.77, 1.05 line losses, oscillation 0.45. Iteration 6 cut base_speed to 0.95 and kd to 0.45. Score fell to 652. Slalom progress dropped to 0.46 and two runs timed out, so the speed cut slowed the robot without fixing the off-track exits. Oscillation fell only slightly (0.45 to 0.37). Speed is therefore not the lever; keep base_speed at 1.1. The sensing change from iteration 4 to 5 was the largest gain, so keep the 7-sensor forward array.

Changes. (1) Restore the iteration 5 controller: base_speed 1.1, kp 3.0, kd 0.5, ki 0, last_direction line loss, same weights. (2) Reduce mass from 0.5 to 0.4 kg, the lower limit. (3) Reduce body_length from 0.15 to 0.12 m. Yaw inertia is mass*(L^2+W^2)/12, so this drops inertia about 25 percent. The robot should turn in and recover faster on slalom direction changes, which is the failure mode. body_width stays 0.12 m, so the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m. Wheel track, radius and sensor layout are unchanged, so this iteration isolates the inertia effect.

Expected result. Slalom progress above 0.85 with fewer line losses (target 0.5 or below). Oval and s-bend should still finish, since the controller is unchanged. Steering oscillation may rise slightly with the faster response.

Hypotheses. (a) Lower yaw inertia reduces overshoot on the slalom's quick direction changes, which cuts line losses. (b) The controller stays fixed, so any gain in slalom progress comes from geometry, not from a change in tuning.

Failure signs. If slalom still ends off-track near progress 0.77 with about 1 line loss, steering authority or sensing is the limit; the next step is a modest kp increase (about 3.3) or a wider array. If oscillation exceeds 0.5, kd should come down toward 0.4.

Next measurements. Progress and line_loss_events on slalom and s-bend show whether inertia helps. steering_oscillation and max_error show gain balance. completion_time on the oval shows the speed margin. noise_robustness is also requested as a check on the disturbance margin.
